title: Newsroom schedule view by day, week and month (FullCalendar)
description:
Part of the scheduled publishing and announcements epic. Design: docs/plans/scheduled-publishing-and-announcements.md ("The schedule view", "Calendar choice").

Goal: a newsroom page "Schedule" shows scheduled, overdue, blocked and recently published Stories by day, week (default) or month, in the publication's time zone, using FullCalendar 7 (`@fullcalendar/react`, MIT) loaded client-only on that page.

Shape: query the `scheduleState+scheduledPublishAt` index for the visible range and the existing `publishedAt` indexes for published items; FullCalendar `timeZone` set to the publication zone; `eventInteractive` so events are focusable; list view by default on screens too narrow for the week grid; border variables set flat; each event shows icon + word + title; a plain list of the same items under the calendar (keyboard and screen-reader path); drag to reschedule calls the reschedule operation (revalidated) with undo; empty state. Spike and evidence: spikes/scheduling-calendar/ and the plan's comparison table.

Depends on: the scheduling backend story.

```gherkin
Feature: Editors see the publishing schedule
  To spread Stories out, editors need to see what is going out when, and what
  already went out, on one page.

  Scenario: The week is the default view
    Given three Stories are scheduled this week and two were published on Monday
    When Sam opens the Schedule page
    Then the current week is shown in New York time
    And each Story shows an icon, its state in words and its title

  Scenario: Switching to day and month
    When Sam chooses "Month"
    Then the whole month is shown with the same items
    And choosing "Day" shows one day by the hour

  Scenario: On a phone the week is a list
    Given Sam opens the page on a screen 375 pixels wide
    Then the week is shown as a list by day
    And nothing scrolls sideways

  Scenario: Keyboard and screen readers have a plain list
    When Sam tabs past the calendar
    Then a list of the same items follows, each with its time, title, state and a link to the Story

  Scenario: Dragging a Story to a new time
    Given a Story scheduled for Thursday 09:00
    When Sam drags it to Friday 10:00
    Then it is rescheduled for Friday 10:00
    And a notice offers "Undo"

  Scenario: Dragging into the past is refused
    When Sam drags a Story to yesterday
    Then it returns to its time with "That time has passed."

  Scenario: Nothing scheduled
    Given nothing is scheduled this week
    Then the page says "Nothing is scheduled this week."
    And offers "Schedule a Story"
```

Open questions: none.
